title: 3am Rapid Handoff Pocket Manual (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, minimal-latency handoff notes for the 3am shift. This is a pocket manual — small, actionable checks and command snippets I actually use when waking up to alerts. Still a draft; lots of TODOs at the bottom.

What I expect incoming to include (ask for these explicitly):
- Current pager summary (who paged, summary sentence, urgency).
- Active incidents and primary contact for each.
- Any ongoing maintenance windows or releases pinned to tomorrow morning.
- Estimated degraded services (latency > x, errors > y).
- Last escalations and why they were suppressed (if they were).

Immediate checks (first 5 minutes):
1) Pager/context: open Slack thread and the JIRA incident. Confirm scope and owner.
   - Command: none, just open links in the incident message.
2) Service health dashboard (console.health.redwood): check error spikes and latency panels for top-3 services.
3) Basic infra sanity: ping control-plane and 1 replica of serving runtime in eu-west-1 and us-west-2.
   - kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide | egrep "serving|router"
   - kubectl -n redwood exec -it <router-pod> -- curl -sS localhost:9000/health || echo "router down"
4) Check autoscaler and queue backlogs: look for scaling events that failed or hit limits.
   - GKE console / k8s-controller logs or: kubectl -n redwood get hpa -o wide
5) Logs: tail the last 100 lines for the primary service and the router.
   - stern serving-202 --since 10m --tail 100

Triage matrix (quick):
- If error rate > 10% and customers impacted: page on-call + escalate to SRE lead + open incident in JIRA.
- If latency regression only (<5% errors): attach to existing incident as "performance" and start a rollback plan.
- If single-region degradation: route traffic to healthy region (policy: failover to dedicated pool in other region) and file capacity ticket.
- If a control-plane component is down: don't do destructive changes. Call the on-call engineer who ran the last deploy (link from deployment history).

Fast fixes (temporary) — use only as stopgaps and record in incident ticket:
- Roll back last deploy if deploy_time < 30m and metrics show jump after deploy.
  - kubectl rollout undo deployment/<service> -n redwood --to-revision=<prev>
- Scale up serving pool (if autoscaler stuck): patch deployment replicas.
  - kubectl scale deployment/<worker-deploy> -n redwood --replicas=12
- Flip traffic to canary fallback model (if model OOMs): console route -> fallback-model-group.

Escalation contacts (order):
1) On-call SRE (current) — Slack: @sre-oncall, phone: +1-555-0138
2) Engineering duty lead — Maya Silva (Slack: @maya), mobile on file
3) Runtime lead — Ethan Brooks (DM on Slack)
4) Product ops (for customer comms) — pager-to-email gateway (prod-comm@redwood.com)

Ticket templates (open fast):
- Title: [INC][<service>] <short symptom> — <region>
- Description: one-liners: "Observed <metric> increase from X->Y between T1 and T2. Impact: <customers/percent>. Recent changes: <deploy/scale/traffic>"
- Tags: incident, <service>, region, pager

Known recurring quick-hits (do these first):
- "router-504-surge" after large batch jobs — restart router pods one at a time and drain connections.
  - kubectl rollout restart deployment/router -n redwood --timeout=5m
- "kvcache-miss-storm" — check cache-hit ratio and temp bump instance count for cache cluster.
- "model-oom-5xx" — fallback to quantized variant, drain node.

Operational notes (less formal):
- If you touch prod routing, keep a 15-min block to observe before doing anything else.
- Use "incident-dump" snippet in Slack to paste the essential diagnostics; save the thread link in JIRA.
- Don't remove long-lived feature flags without a safety net — they're often stabilizers for old clients.

Post-incident chores (short checklist):
- Add a short root-cause header in the incident ticket within 2 hours.
- Update the affected service's monitoring dashboard to add a 1-min rollup panel if it was missing.
- If we rolled back a model, add a follow-up task to test the model changes in staging with load tests.
- Quick blurb for product: "We saw elevated X; we mitigated by Y. Customers affected: Z; next steps..."

Shortcuts I use (keep inside clipboard):
- kubectl aliases: k=kubectl; kx="kubectl -n redwood"
- Dump logs to S3 helper: ./scripts/dump-incident-logs.sh --since 2h --service serving | aws s3 cp - s3://incidents/<id>/logs.txt

Unresolved / TODOs (things to improve in this doc):
- Add an explicit perf-baseline snapshot command (quick delta between last 30m and 24h).
- Better one-click traffic-swap UI link (file ticket: INFRA-1109).
- Consolidate regional failover play into a single script and document args.

Notes to self (personal):
- I always forget the exact HPA metric key name; pin that into the k8s alias file.
- If I wake up groggy, do the checklist in order: pager -> dashboard -> logs -> minimal action. Resist temptation to full diagnose live.

If you pick this up from another on-call: leave a one-sentence status at top of the Slack thread and ping next on-call with the incident link.

End of pocket manual. Keep it clipped and accessible on phone home screen.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-02: initial draft (Noah)
- 2025-12-10: added ticket templates + fast fixes (Maya)
- 2026-01-15: updated escalation order and short commands (Ethan)

---
Plain TODOs (for later cleanup):

- Add screenshots for console steps where routing flip is done.
